paths.path: ~/.config/dosbox/dosbox-staging.conf (primary config with global settings; other common XDG locations are also looked up on Linux; found via --printconf, edited via --editconf, recreated with defaults via --eraseconf). Additionally a local per-game config named dosbox.conf in the startup/working directory is loaded after the primary config; the [autoexec] section must be last. Portable mode: an empty dosbox-staging.conf beside the executable makes that folder the config root. Settings are plain text section/key=value, editable at runtime via CONFIG -set.
evidence: docs:website/docs/0.83/manual/using-dosbox-staging/configuration.md @d9135010ea (path table row Linux ~/.config/dosbox/dosbox-staging.conf, XDG lookup note, local config, portable mode)

paths.path: Controller config is the [sdl] mapperfile setting pointing at a mapper file - by default mapper-sdl2-<version>.map stored alongside the primary config (i.e. ~/.config/dosbox/). Mapper files are plain text; each line maps an event name to one or more bindings: event_name "binding_1" "binding_2", e.g. key_esc "key 41" "stick_0 button 6"; keyboard bindings are key <scancode> with optional mod1/mod2/mod3 modifiers. Pre-configured per-game profiles ship in resources/mapperfiles and are loaded by name (mapperfile = xbox/doom.map). --erasemapper deletes only the default mapper file.
paths.naming: mapper-sdl2-<version>.map by default; plain-text event_name "binding" lines, or a bundled resources/mapperfiles profile name
evidence: source:src/gui/mapper.cpp + src/gui/mapper.h contain the mapperfile handling (code-search hit for 'mapperfile' @main)

paths.path: No emulator-managed save files exist: game saves are ordinary files that the DOS program writes inside whatever is mounted. Save data therefore lives in the mounted game directory (mount C ~/dosgames/...) or inside the mounted disk image itself (floppy/CD/hard-disk images via MOUNT/IMGMOUNT) - copying or backing up the image/directory backs up the saves. 0.83 deprecates IMGMOUNT in favour of MOUNT for both directories and disk images, and supports overlay mounts (mount C /path/to/saves -t overlay) so a game can keep saving while the pristine base image stays untouched.
paths.naming: Determined by the DOS game, not the emulator: e.g. SAVEGAME.* / *.SAV files created inside the mounted drive or inside the .img/.ima/.ima/.vhd/.hdf disk image; Staging applies no naming of its own
evidence: docs:website/docs/0.83/manual/using-dosbox-staging/storage.md @d9135010ea (mounting directories or disk images, automount, 'while still allowing the game to save data: mount C /path/to/saves -t overlay', 'IMGMOUNT is deprecated. Use MOUNT for both directories and disk images')

paths.path: None - DOSBox Staging has no save-state feature and declined to add one (upstream issue #313 'Save States support' closed 2024-09-29 with state_reason not_planned, label "won't do"). The only capture flows are media captures: Ctrl+F5 screenshot, Ctrl+F6 audio recording, Ctrl+F7 video recording, written to the [capture] folder which defaults to 'capture' in the current working directory. There is no CAPS-key or other state-capture mechanism.
paths.naming: n/a - no states; capture artifacts are named by the emulator inside the capture folder (screenshots/audio/video)
